inheritedAnchors.sourceQuote: SHOULD / SHOULD NOT — required by default. A deviation is permitted only when a concrete technical constraint makes the requirement unsuitable for that exact case; the implementation MUST record the exception, reason, affected scope, fallback behaviour and validation evidence.
Lowercase uses of “must”, “should” and “may” have the same normative meaning. Product prose MUST NOT use “should” merely to mean “it would be nice if”.

A specification exception MUST identify: requirement ID or quoted requirement, affected product/version/platform, technical reason, exact substitute behaviour, user-visible impact, security/data impact, tests/evidence and whether the exception is temporary or permanent. “Too difficult”, “not enough time”, “donor source unavailable” or “not implemented yet” are not valid permanent exceptions.

Completion evidence MUST cover representative end-to-end journeys, persistence/restart behaviour, API/UI parity, permissions, accessibility, failure/recovery paths, donor parity where applicable and platform/package validation for every declared supported platform.
Known failing requirements MUST remain explicitly recorded as open blockers or scoped exceptions. They MUST NOT be omitted from release/completion reporting.

All work must be accessible. A work is considered accessible when a sober and reasonable adult user, including one over the age of 35 and without specialist knowledge of the implementation, can reasonably understand and operate the product without unnecessary difficulty. Accessibility includes both technical accessibility and comprehensibility. Where applicable, the agent should account for:

Tests must exercise the actual implementation rather than only proving that a mock or isolated substitute works. Where a full test suite cannot run because of an environmental limitation, the agent must run the strongest relevant subset available and clearly identify the remaining unverified gate. A pre-existing unrelated failure must not automatically invalidate otherwise valid work, but it must be distinguished from failures caused by the current changes.

Where a project supports multiple operating systems, architectures, browsers, devices, or runtime environments, changes must account for the supported matrix. The agent must not unknowingly introduce a dependency on the environment it personally used for development. Platform-specific behaviour should be isolated where appropriate. Where comprehensive multi-platform testing is unavailable, affected platforms must be identified as unverified rather than implicitly claimed as validated.

Donor parity is mandatory. If a 9to1 app is based on a donor application/project, all donor features, user-visible behaviours and quality-of-life improvements must be ported unless technically impossible and explicitly documented. Proprietary donor AI features are the exception: replace them with equivalent 9to1 AI capabilities rather than porting the proprietary AI.

Where an app declares a donor/upstream project, the implementation MUST contain the actual donor source (forked, vendored or otherwise included according to the repository architecture) in the app’s source tree/build graph. Runtime installation MUST NOT require the user to separately download the donor application merely to obtain donor functionality. The selected donor revision/version and local modifications MUST be traceable.

Cross-app examples are acceptance criteria, not optional demos. Examples include live Canvas pages inside Boards, Files-hosted documents edited from Spaces, Maps routes attached to Planner events, and app-to-app Automation workflows.

Verification means real behaviour. Source presence or a successful build alone is never enough; parity, interaction, accessibility, platform/package and representative end-to-end journeys must be evidenced.

A desktop-only feature is not sufficient reason to omit an otherwise useful web app. Mini Computer retains its existing web exemption unless the required hosted-compute capability is explicitly provided. Other missing native capabilities MUST NOT be represented as available merely because a browser interface exists.

Release-candidate AI Studio implementations MUST NOT expose Training Lab as an in-scope project type, navigation/sidebar entry, New Project option or partially functional placeholder. Future implementation requires a separate canonical specification before Training Lab becomes in scope.
